Sheriff's department gives update on Nancy Guthrie case 9 months after kidnapping

The Pima County Sheriff’s Department gave an update in the Nancy Guthrie missing person’s case Friday, saying the department continuing to work to advance the case.

Actual Article Body:
This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed. ©2026 FOX News Network, LLC. All rights reserved. Quotes displayed in real-time or delayed by at least 15 minutes. Market data provided by Factset. Powered and implemented by FactSet Digital Solutions. Legal Statement. Mutual Fund and ETF data provided by LSEG.

Lisa Miller, a retired detective and law enforcement executive with the Colorado Attorney General's Office, breaks down some of the unique attributes of the purported ransom note.

The Pima County Sheriff’s Department gave an update on the Nancy Guthrie missing person’s case Friday, saying the department continues to work with the Nancy Guthrie Task Force on DNA analysis in an effort to advance the case.

"Earlier this month, investigators traveled to Florida to meet with lab scientists to see what more could be done to advance this case," the department wrote in an X post. "A number of ideas were discussed, and we continue to work with all our partners to solve this case."

The law enforcement agency reminded the public that no tip is too small.

"Even the smallest piece of information could be critical to this investigation," the department said.

NANCY GUTHRIE CASE: UNCLAIMED $1.2M REWARD SUGGESTS 'VERY SMALL CIRCLE' OF SUSPECTS, RETIRED FBI AGENT SAYS

Savannah Guthrie poses alongside her mother Nancy Guthrie during a production break while hosting NBC's "Today Show."  ( Don Arnold/WireImage)

Guthrie, NBC journalist Savannah Guthrie’s mother, was kidnapped from her home in Tucson, Arizona, on Feb. 1.

The 84-year-old was last seen shortly before 10 p.m. Jan. 31 after a relative dropped her off at her home in the Catalina Foothills neighborhood of Tucson.

Authorities have struggled to identify a suspect or person of interest in her disappearance despite a masked man appearing on Guthrie's Ring doorbell camera.

Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos, in the days following Guthrie's disappearance, confirmed that she was taken, telling reporters during a news briefing, "She did not leave on her own. We know that."

NANCY GUTHRIE INVESTIGATORS SEE UPTICK IN TIPS AFTER RANSOM NOTES RELEASE: SHERIFF

Authorities previously released two ransom notes related to Guthrie's kidnapping in July.

A split image shows a group of Pima County deputies investigating outside the home of Nancy Guthrie in Tucson, Arizona, and a portrait of Guthrie. She has been missing since Feb. 1, when she is believed to have been abducted from her house. (Michael Ruiz/Fox News Digital; Courtesy of NBC)

The first, which was sent Feb. 2, reported that Guthrie was unharmed and demanded that her captors be sent $4 million in cryptocurrency to secure her release.

NANCY GUTHRIE RANSOM NOTES MAY BE FAKE AS RENOWNED PROFILER SAYS CASE LOOKS MORE LIKE BURGLARY GONE WRONG

The second, sent four days later on Feb. 6, said Guthrie had died shortly after she was kidnapped.

Authorities released the ransom notes in late July, noting they were written with a unique writing style, asking anyone who recognizes the patterns to share any information with PCSD and the FBI.

A photograph of Nancy Guthrie is seen on a sign that people can leave messages on February 26, 2026, in Tucson, Arizona. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

Late last month, investigators said they had been made aware of a possible new ransom note in relation to Guthrie's disappearance.

"The PCSD/FBI Guthrie Task Force was recently made aware of a new possible ransom note related to the Nancy Guthrie investigation," PCSD wrote in an X post in late September.

"Investigators are also aware of social media comments regarding the note and are looking further into the information to determine its credibility."

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Anyone with information is asked to dial 1-800-CALL-FBI or, to remain anonymous, call 520-88-CRIME.

Fox News' Robert McGreevy contributed to this report.

Cuba Gives Hero's Welcome to Thug 'Diplomat' Expelled from America for U.N. Attack

Regime officials in Cuba staged a warm welcome on Thursday for Richard Tur, a former member of the country's United Nations delegation who was expelled from America this week after attacking U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz's spokesman.
The post Cuba Gives Hero’s Welcome to Thug ‘Diplomat’ Expelled from America for U.N. Attack appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
Regime officials in Cuba staged a warm welcome on Thursday for Richard Tur, a former member of the country’s United Nations delegation who was expelled from America this week after attacking U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz’s spokesman.

The altercation occurred in the context of one of several attempts by the communist delegation to disrupt Ambassador Waltz and other speakers denouncing human rights abuses and corruption by the Cuban regime at the United Nations this month in anticipation of a symbolic annual vote to condemn the alleged American “embargo” on Cuba.

Cuban “diplomats” staged several attempts at “acts of repudiation,” mob scenes commonly used on the island to harass and humiliate political dissidents, including one on the floor of the General Assembly. Foreign Minister Bruno Rodríguez participated in these acts of repudiation, attempting to shout down Ambassador Waltz while he spoke at the General Assembly podium, but Tur was the only one caught on camera engaging in an active assault of a member of the American delegation, Waltz spokesman J.P. Freire.

Freire shared a video on Tuesday of Tur approaching him at the General Assembly and attempting to snatch his phone out of his hand.

“The Castro regime once again sought to intimidate clerks into cutting off [Waltz’s] mic for showing the world the dictatorship’s hypocrisy and wealth at the expense of the Cuban people,” he explained, referring to the ambassador’s address before the General Assembly. “After this guy went after me for recording him in the U.N. GENERAL ASSEMBLY, this violent foreign Leftist said that if I did this in NYC streets he would have the right to sue me as violating his PRIVACY.”

“1. His own team was recording throughout the chamber. Strange to think he felt I was violating his privacy. 2. As the Cuban mission attempts to silence criticism of the Castro regime’s abuse and wealth, they want to avail themselves of American rights they don’t even understand,” he concluded.

Waltz confirmed on television on Wednesday that Secretary of State Marco Rubio had approved the expulsion of Tur from the country for the attack.

“Just before I came on tonight, Secretary Rubio signed the paperwork to eject the diplomat that thought he could — the Cuban diplomat, the first secretary of their delegation, who shoved and tried to assault one of our American diplomats. He’s gone,” he explained. “You lay a hand on an American here in the United States, President Trump, Secretary Rubio, and myself, we’re not going to stand for it. There will be consequences.”

First Viceminister Gerardo Peñalver Portal of Cuba’s Ministry of External Relations (Minrex) confirmed Tur’s return home, treating him as a hero who valiantly stood up against American imperialism and notably omitting any mention of his physical attack.

“We received in the nation the young diplomat… who in a firm and dignified manner faced the disrespectful and provocative attitude of the U.S. delegation,” Peñalver claimed, sharing a photo on social media of a group of regime officials welcoming Tur home with a large Cuban flag.

Peñalver accused American officials of engaging in a “strategy to hamper the vote on the resolution against the genocidal blockade and Richard Tur’s candidacy to an important organ of the United Nations.”

The Cuban delegation is attempting to pitch Tur for a position on an administrative body, the Consultative Commission on Administrative and Budgeting Matters, in the 2027 to 2029 term. Denying him entry to the United States would likely make holding such a position more of a challenge, but it is not clear at press time whether his nomination is impacted in any way by the assault incident. Peñalver notably omitted his attack on a fellow diplomat from his effusive welcome message to the junior official.

The independent outlet Diario de Cuba observed in its coverage of the incident that Tur is a member of one of the Castro regime’s most elite families, the son of longtime regime diplomat Ricardo Tur Novo and husband to a fellow member of the Cuban United Nations delegation. Serving as a diplomat abroad allows Castro regime elites to avoid the consequences of their rule, which has plunged Cuba into abject poverty for decades. Since January, following the American arrest of Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro, Cuba has not had access to the free or heavily discounted Venezuelan oil typically used to help the Cuban wealthy fuel their electric generators, which allowed them to avoid living with the routine blackouts in the country as a result of the government’s refusal to engage in any meaningful maintenance of the power grid.

The incidents at the U.N. occurred in anticipation of a vote to condemn the U.S. “embargo” — in reality a series of American economic limitations to keep money out of the Castro regime’s pockets that does not affect access to American food or humanitarian aid. The U.N. has hosted the symbolic vote at the regime’s request since the early 1990s, in previous years securing near unanimous support for condemning America. On Wednesday, Cuba received the smallest number of votes for its resolution. Only 130 countries voted for the resolution, down from 165 countries just a year ago, and a record number either voted against the resolution or abstained from the vote.
